name: Lunokhod 1 rover (with its Luna 17 lander)

location.name: Mare Imbrium (Sea of Rains), Lunokhod 1's final parking place

headline: The first rover to drive on another world, lost for decades, then found from orbit
story: At 03:46:50 UT on 17 November 1970, the Soviet lander Luna 17 settled onto Mare Imbrium, the Sea of Rains. Less than three hours later an eight-wheeled machine rolled down its ramp. Lunokhod 1 became the first rover to drive on another world, steered by a five-man crew on Earth who worked through a delay of at least four seconds.

Built to last three lunar days, it worked through eleven. It drove about 10.5 kilometres, sent home more than 20,000 television images, tested the soil at more than 500 spots and carried a French laser reflector. The last communication session ended on 14 September 1971. On 4 October, controllers stopped trying to reach it.

For almost four decades, no one knew exactly where it had stopped. In 2010, NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter photographed the lander, the rover and their tracks, and a laser team in New Mexico found its reflector again. Lunokhod 1 still sits north of Luna 17, and scientists aim lasers at it to study the Moon.
